hook: The sea dog who sailed around the world: a hero in England, a pirate in Spain.

pages.x: Francis Drake was born around 1540 near Tavistock, in Devon. He went to sea young, and sailed with his cousin John Hawkins on slave-trading voyages between Africa and the Caribbean. In 1568 the Spanish ambushed their fleet in Mexico, and Drake swore revenge.

In 1573 he raided the Spanish mule trains carrying silver across Panama, with escaped slaves called Cimarrons as his allies, and came home rich. From a tree on a hilltop he saw the Pacific, and prayed to sail an English ship on it.

From 1577 to 1580 he sailed around the world in the Golden Hind, the first captain to do it in his own ship and live. He raided Spanish ports in Chile and Peru, captured a treasure ship, landed in California, and came home loaded with silver.
Queen Elizabeth, who had secretly backed the voyage, came aboard the Golden Hind and knighted him on the deck. Spain called him a pirate, El Draque, "the dragon".
In 1587 he sailed into Cádiz harbour and destroyed about 30 Spanish ships being readied for the Armada, delaying it by a year. He called it "singeing the King of Spain's beard".

When the Armada was sighted in 1588, legend says Drake was playing bowls on Plymouth Hoe and insisted on finishing the game: there was time to win it and beat the Spaniards too. Days later his fireships broke up the Armada at night.
He died of dysentery in 1596 off Panama, on a last raid, and was buried at sea in a lead coffin, which divers still hope to find.
Drake was the first Englishman to sail around the world. His raids and his part in beating the Armada helped make England a sea power, though his career began in the slave trade.
